purpose: Establish (a) whether exeris-community's recommendation traversal could match anything in the seeded Neo4j graph, and (b) the mechanism behind its Neo4j CPU and cart-read latency. Read-only Cypher against the live container; no run, no mutation.
provenance_caveat: Probed AFTER the campaign, against the graph state left by the last run on the box (spring-hibernate rep-3 re-run: 17369 User nodes = 1000 seeded + 16369 registered; 16369 IN_CART edges = that rep's iteration count; all ids integer). Relationship-TYPE and node-KEY findings transfer regardless, because both are properties of the seed script, which is unchanged and hash-pinned in run-metadata.infra_contract.seed_overlay. What this state canNOT show is what exeris's own IN_CART writes looked like during its reps.

a_edge_type_mismatch.finding: The relationship type exeris-community traverses on hop 1 does not exist in the Neo4j track.
a_edge_type_mismatch.probe: CALL db.relationshipTypes() YIELD relationshipType RETURN relationshipType
a_edge_type_mismatch.note: BOUGHT exists only in runtime/db/seed/v4_pgq_graph.sql, i.e. the PGQ backend, not the neo4j graph_track this campaign pinned. Direction differs as well: seed writes Product->User, adapter asks User->Product.

b_node_key_mismatch.finding: Independent of (a): node identity does not match. Either mismatch alone is sufficient to make hop 1 return empty.
b_node_key_mismatch.probe: MATCH (n) WHERE n.id IS NOT NULL AND toString(n.id) CONTAINS "-" RETURN count(n)

c_silent_fallback.finding: Empty hop 1 is not an error path — it is silently absorbed, which is why the defect survived a full campaign.
c_silent_fallback.adapter_behaviour: GraphShopAdapter.java:48-50 — if (purchasedProducts.isEmpty()) return List.of(); the N loop never starts
c_silent_fallback.service_behaviour: catch (RuntimeException ignored) {} plus an empty-ids fall-through; both routes end at productRepository.findRecommendedForUser(userId, limit) in Postgres
c_silent_fallback.consequence: recommend_latency_ms for exeris-community = one fruitless Neo4j lookup + a Postgres recommendation query; for quarkus/spring = a working two-hop Cypher recommendation. Not comparable in any sense, platform-natural included.
c_silent_fallback.consequence_cpu: Part of exeris's +1.4 ms/saga Postgres CPU over the Axon stacks is this fallback query, which neither Axon stack issues.

d_scan_vs_seek_profile.finding: The mechanism behind the Neo4j CPU and the cart-read latency is an unlabelled traversal anchor, not query count. Labels alone account for the entire db-hit difference; the redundant path binding accounts for none of it.
d_scan_vs_seek_profile.emitted_shape_attribution: Shape A/A2 reconstructed from a reading of CommunityGraphDialect.buildMultiHopQuery (exeris-kernel source, NOT present in this repository). The db-hit measurements below are ours; the claim that the dialect emits this shape is attributed, not verified here.

shapes.label: unlabelled anchor + MATCH p= (as emitted)
shapes.cypher: PROFILE MATCH p = (source)-[:IN_CART*1..1]->(target) WHERE source.id = 1262 RETURN DISTINCT target.id AS id

shapes.label: unlabelled anchor, no path binding
shapes.cypher: PROFILE MATCH (source)-[:IN_CART*1..1]->(target) WHERE source.id = 1262 RETURN DISTINCT target.id AS id

shapes.label: labelled anchor, path binding retained
shapes.cypher: PROFILE MATCH p = (source:User)-[:IN_CART*1..1]->(target:Product) WHERE source.id = 1262 RETURN DISTINCT target.id AS id

shapes.label: label-scoped seek (quarkus/spring shape)
shapes.cypher: PROFILE MATCH (u:User {id: 1262})-[:IN_CART]->(pr:Product) RETURN pr.id AS id

decomposition.labels_cost_ratio: A2 vs A3 = 35742 / 6 = 5957x — the whole effect
decomposition.path_binding_cost: A vs A2 = 35742 / 35742 = 1.00x — zero db hits
decomposition.fix: Emit the sourceNode()/targetNode() labels the descriptor already carries. Dropping MATCH p= is worth doing for allocation but is measurably not the lever.

d_scan_vs_seek_profile.why_seek_is_impossible_without_labels: Neo4j indexes are label-scoped, including the seed's own user_id_unique / product_id_unique constraints (seed-neo4j-from-postgres.sh:183-184). An unlabelled anchor cannot use them, so the plan degrades to a scan + filter.
caveats: db hits are not a wall-clock model: a 5957x db-hit ratio produced a 5.5x cart-read latency ratio, because the traversal is a small part of a request that also does HTTP, JSON and a Postgres cart read.
The scan cost is not constant during a run: the graph grew by ~16400 User nodes and ~16400 IN_CART edges per rep, so a scanning plan degrades over the window while a seek does not.
Probed with integer ids so both shapes can actually match, isolating the planner effect from the key mismatch in (b).

e_why_cart_read_is_the_controlled_compar.finding: cart-get isolates the planner effect: same query count, same discard-and-serve-from-Postgres shape, self-consistent keys on both sides.
e_why_cart_read_is_the_controlled_compar.exeris: RepositoryBackedBenchmarkUseCaseService.getCart — graphShopAdapter.readCartProductNodeIds(userId) inside try/catch(RuntimeException ignored), result DISCARDED, view served from cartRepository.getCart(userId)
e_why_cart_read_is_the_controlled_compar.quarkus: ShopSagaStateService.getOrCreateCart — graphShopService.cartProductIds(uid), result DISCARDED, view served from buildCartView(conn, uid)
e_why_cart_read_is_the_controlled_compar.round_trips: one per stack; no N+1 on either side (single-hop over one edge type, which the SPI expresses well)
e_why_cart_read_is_the_controlled_compar.exeris_self_consistency: writer and reader both key by UUID, so unlike the recommendation path the cart traversal does find its own edges

unaffected_by_this_defect: Saga latency (report section 3): POST /api/v1/orders touches no graph in any of the three apps — all three call their graph adapter at exactly three sites (recommend, cart-add upsert, cart-get read).
Footprint (report section 6): the defect costs CPU and latency, not resident memory.
Correctness gate: 497/497 in all nine reps, independent of the graph path.
quarkus-hibernate vs spring-hibernate cost comparison: both run the working graph path.
invalidated_by_this_defect: Every exeris-vs-* cost comparison (target-JVM CPU, Postgres CPU, Neo4j CPU, whole-deployment total).
recommend_latency_ms as a cross-stack row, in any sense including platform-natural.
CONTRACT-v2 section 2's stated mechanism for exeris's Neo4j cost, and its 2.6x / 2.5x figures.
